findings.hypothesis: There is a large overall drop between created and confirmed (64.52% of created orders lost). This pattern is correlated with broad checkout friction or buyer second thoughts across the catalog rather than a small technical artifact visible in the delivered stage.
findings.confirm_via: Run a randomized experiment that applies a generic friction-reduction treatment (e.g., persistent cart + one-click confirm flow + clearer price/fees summary) vs control across all users and measure change in created->confirmed conversion. If the treatment increases conversion materially relative to control, this supports the friction hypothesis.

findings.hypothesis: Most captured reasons for the created->confirmed loss are user-initiated (user_total 199417) rather than artifact issues (artifact_total 42107), suggesting user behavior (cart abandonment / navigation away) is a major correlate of the gap. However, the reason clusters sum (199417 + 42107 = 241524) explains only part of the total lost (417569), so other uncaptured reasons are also present.
findings.confirm_via: Drill down by product segment (or run targeted experiments per segment) to see whether user-initiated abandonment concentrates in specific product categories or price bands. Alternatively, run an experiment showing tailored recovery nudges (e.g., exit intent / persistent cart reminders) to a random subset of users who start checkout; measure whether confirmed counts increase relative to control to validate that user-initiated abandonment is addressable.

next_question.rationale: We need to localize where the unexplained losses and the heavy user-initiated abandons are concentrated. Breaking the created->confirmed funnel and reason clusters down by pd_category will show whether a few product categories drive most of the drop (and whether those categories align with user abandon reasons), which informs whether product-targeted fixes (inventory, pricing, content, consultation prompts) or broad UX fixes are the right priority.
